title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics
summary_box: India Glycols' integrated Kashipur and Gorakhpur hubs sit inside North India's sugarcane and grain belt. That location feeds a pipeline-linked Bio-EO ecosystem and export-oriented glycol ether logistics. On audited FY26 pre-demerger numbers (₹4,211 Cr revenue), EBITDA margin reached 15.4% and CFO hit ₹769 Cr (122% CFO/EBITDA). However, ₹816 Cr of capex kept FCF at -₹47 Cr. Post-demerger Q1–Q2 FY27 continuing operations show 11% OPM, while interest and depreciation each dropped by ~70%–75% to ₹12 Cr/quarter.

epigraph.quote: In process chemicals, geography is margin: every kilometer you haul wet biomass or corrosive ethylene oxide eats the spread before the molecule ever reaches a customer.
epigraph.author: Chemical Plant Economics Principle

web_blocks.html: India Glycols' physical supply chain rests on two integrated complexes: a 300-acre flagship site in Kashipur (Uttarakhand) and a complementary facility in Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh) [10][12][19]. Locating in the Terai sugarcane and Gangetic grain belt solves the first-mile logistics problem of bio-chemistry. Rather than railing bulky molasses or grain across India, IGL ferments regional agricultural feedstocks into ethanol on-site. It then dehydrates that ethanol into bio-ethylene and oxidizes it in air-separation-backed reactors into Bio-Ethylene Oxide (Bio-EO) [10][12].

From that central Bio-EO node, distribution splits into three distinct channels. First is pipeline-integrated JV offtake, where IGL pipes Bio-EO across the fence at Kashipur to Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals Pvt Ltd under long-term contracts [10][11]. Second is domestic and export ISO-tank and drum logistics for Bio-MEG, Bio-DEG, Bio-TEG, and higher-margin Glycol Ethers & Acetates. Those shipments serve European, Asian, and Indian coatings, brake-fluid, textile, and packaging buyers [6][10][19]. Third is regional cryogenic tanker and cylinder distribution for Industrial Gases and IGL-SteriGas across North Indian hospitals and medical-device clusters [12].

web_blocks.takeaway: In its final pre-demerger audited year (FY26), IGL converted ₹4,211 Cr of sales into ₹649 Cr EBITDA (15.4%) and ₹769 Cr CFO (18.3% of sales). However, ₹816 Cr of expansion capex left Free Cash Flow at -₹47 Cr.

web_blocks.html: Two forensic nuances stand out in the FY26 waterfall and the Q1–Q2 FY27 transition. First, capital intensity was the primary drag on free cash flow across FY22–FY26. IGL invested heavily in grain-based distillery and ethanol capacity, which now sits inside IGL Spirits Ltd. That capex produced negative FCF for five straight years: -₹264 Cr in FY22, -₹109 Cr in FY23, -₹103 Cr in FY24, -₹391 Cr in FY25, and -₹47 Cr in FY26, even as operating cash flow recovered to ₹769 Cr in FY26 [1][12]. Second, working capital discipline improved markedly. Debtor Days fell from 59 days in FY23 to 30 days in FY26, while Inventory Days compressed from 224 days in FY24 to 139 days in FY26. That kept the Cash Conversion Cycle at 47 days and Working Capital Days negative (-49 days) [1].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Look closely at the two halves of the unit-economics story. Pre-demerger, IGL looked like a cash-burning capex machine (-₹391 Cr FCF in FY25) because it was building large grain distilleries for ethanol. Those distilleries and ₹865 Cr of accompanying borrowings have now been carved out into IGL Spirits.

What remains in INDIAGLYCO is a much lighter asset base (Fixed Assets ₹1,257 Cr at Sep 2026 vs. ₹4,554 Cr at Mar 2026), with quarterly interest down from ₹49 Cr to ₹12 Cr. Over FY27–FY28, BSPC must sustain >12%–14% OPM without heavy maintenance capex. Only then will accounting profit turn into genuine free cash flow.

book_paragraphs: Walk through the Kashipur plant gates with me and follow a single molecule of sugar from field to export container. In the Terai belt surrounding Kashipur, local sugar mills crush cane and sell molasses—a thick, dark byproduct—at prices governed by state agricultural policy and ethanol demand. India Glycols ferments that molasses into industrial alcohol, strips out water to make bio-ethylene, and feeds it alongside oxygen from its own Air Separation Unit into an ethylene oxide reactor.

Why does that physical integration matter for your unit economics? Because ethylene oxide is volatile, hazardous, and virtually impossible to ship long distances economically. By piping Bio-EO directly across the fence to the Clariant IGL joint venture, India Glycols turns a dangerous intermediate into a captive tollbooth. Meanwhile, the remaining Bio-EO flows into Bio-MEG, glycol ethers, and IGL-SteriGas medical sterilization cylinders.

On the pre-demerger audited numbers for FY26, every ₹100 of revenue across the combined group absorbed ₹84.60 in operating expenses—roughly ₹63.60 in raw materials, ₹4.60 in employee costs, and ₹16.30 in power, fuel, and other overheads—leaving ₹15.40 in EBITDA. Depreciation took ₹3.70 and interest took nearly ₹4.00, while ₹1.20 of other income lifted pre-tax profit to ₹8.95 and net profit to ₹6.96.

The catch was always below the operating line in cash flow. In FY26, India Glycols generated a stellar ₹769 Cr in operating cash flow, helped by cutting inventory days from 209 to 139. Yet it spent ₹816 Cr on capex—mostly expanding distilleries—leaving free cash flow at minus ₹47 Cr.

Now look at the first six months of FY27 after the demerger boundary took effect on April 1, 2026. Continuing revenue ran at ₹357 Cr in Q1 and ₹362 Cr in Q2, with operating margins settling at 11%. Crucially, quarterly interest dropped from ₹49 Cr a year ago to just ₹12 Cr, and quarterly depreciation fell from ₹41 Cr to ₹12 Cr. The heavy distillery capex cycle has left the building; what remains is a leaner chemical complex whose job is finally to mint free cash.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Negative working capital days (-49 days in FY26) and 30-day receivables show that IGL collects cash faster than it pays suppliers. Now that the capital-hungry biofuel expansion sits in a separate company, watch whether capex stays well below depreciation plus retained earnings.
